hyps.why: Deleting a conv3x3 edge removes real learned capacity (runs 41, 50, 96 all drop, run 96 catastrophically), whereas deleting a weak op does not hurt.
Removing a conv3x3 on the edge into the output node costs accuracy (runs 51, 75), while removing a parameter-free skip there does not.
Replacing a conv3x3 with a parameter-free skip loses feature extraction (runs 55, 71, 79 all negative).
Filling an empty direct input-to-output edge with a skip adds a gradient path and helps (runs 62, 66), whereas replacing an existing op with skip is neutral or harmful.
Upgrading a parameter-free skip on the output edge to conv3x3 gives a much larger gain than upgrading any other op (run 53 vs runs 52, 56, 57, 58, 60).
Removing the direct input-to-output conv3x3 hurts all datasets, especially ImageNet16 (run 65).
Swapping a conv3x3 for a pooling op reduces learnable capacity (run 91), unlike swapping in pool for a weaker op.
Replacing the final conv3x3 with parameter-free pooling clearly degrades accuracy (run 59).
Removing a pooling edge, which is a poor feature extractor, helps (run 94) while removing a conv hurts.
Dropping a parameter-free skip on the output edge costs nothing and can help (run 73), unlike dropping a conv (runs 51, 75).
